question:
A 64-year-old man with a history of smoking undergoes resection of an isolated 2-cm bladder tumor.
CT imaging demonstrates no upper tract involvement. Which surveillance protocol would be most
appropriate for this patient? Answer Choices: (A) Cystoscopy at 3 months, 6-9 months, then annually,
and no upper tract imaging (B) Cystoscopy every 3 months for 2 years, then every 6 months, with
annual upper tract imaging (C) Annual cystoscopy with CT urogram every 2 years (D) Semi-annual
cystoscopy with cytology and no upper tract imaging (E) Cystoscopy every 4 months for 2 years, then
annually with upper tract imaging every 3 years (F) Cystoscopy and cytology every 6 months with
biannual upper tract imaging (G) Cystoscopy or urine cytology at 3 months then every 6 months, and
upper tract imaging every 1-2 years (H) Cystoscopy at 3 months then every 6 months, and upper tract
imaging every 1-2 years (I) Quarterly cystoscopy for one year, then semi-annually with no upper tract
imaging (J) Cystoscopy at 1 month, 3 months, then annually with biennial upper tract imaging
 A. Cystoscopy at 3 months then every 6 months, and upper tract imaging every 1-2 years
B. Quarterly cystoscopy for one year, then semi-annually with no upper tract imaging
C. Semi-annual cystoscopy with cytology and no upper tract imaging
D. Cystoscopy every 3 months for 2 years, then every 6 months, with annual upper tract imaging
E. Cystoscopy at 3 months, 6-9 months, then annually, and no upper tract imaging
F. Cystoscopy or urine cytology at 3 months then every 6 months, and upper tract imaging every 1-2
years
G. Cystoscopy every 4 months for 2 years, then annually with upper tract imaging every 3 years
H. Annual cystoscopy with CT urogram every 2 years
I. Cystoscopy and cytology every 6 months with biannual upper tract imaging
J. Cystoscopy at 1 month, 3 months, then annually with biennial upper tract imaging
